sources.title: Maṇimēkalai · English translation by Kausalya Hart
sources.edition: Project Madurai Unicode text; English translation by Kausalya Hart
sources.locator: Cantos 15–26 (Hart canto and line numbering; selected cited lines)

claims.subject: tamil_later_saduvan
claims.summary: Kāyasandihai’s embedded story identifies Sāduvan as Āthirai’s husband; he leaves her for an unnamed courtesan.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai in quoted speech
claims.note: The courtesan is unnamed and is not made a person node.

claims.subject: tamil_later_saduvan
claims.summary: After the shipwreck, Sāduvan reaches Naga country; Sāranars take him to their leader Gurumahan, who shelters him.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai recounting the story
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_nakka_saranar_group
claims.summary: The Nakka Sāranars tell Sāduvan their leader Gurumahan is present and bring him to the leader.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai recounting the story
claims.note: The passage uses the plural “Nakka Sāranars” for the people who bring Sāduvan to Gurumahan; kept distinct from the named Nakka Saranar Nāgar mentioned in the voice to Āthirai.

claims.subject: tamil_later_saduvan
claims.summary: Sāduvan speaks with Gurumahan, becomes his friend, and explains his account of rebirth and conduct.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai recounting the story
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_gurumahan
claims.summary: Gurumahan orders his men to provide a young woman, meat, and toddy; Sāduvan refuses the offered items.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai recounting the story
claims.note: The account records an offer and refusal, not that Sāduvan accepted these things.

claims.subject: tamil_later_gurumahan
claims.summary: After Sāduvan teaches him not to kill shipwreck survivors, Gurumahan agrees to follow the advice and gives Sāduvan goods.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai recounting the story
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_chandradathan
claims.summary: The merchant Chandradathan arrives on the island, and Sāduvan sails with him back home.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai recounting the story
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_saduvan
claims.summary: After returning with Chandradathan, Sāduvan lives with Āthirai and performs charitable acts.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai recounting the story
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_athirai
claims.summary: At Kāyasandihai’s direction, the heroine accepts alms from Āthirai, who gives food from the Amudhasurabhi.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_manimekalai_heroine
claims.summary: Manimekalai gives food from the Amudhasurabhi to Kāyasandihai, appeasing her insatiable hunger.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_viruchigan
claims.summary: Kāyasandihai says sage Viruchigan cursed her with insatiable hunger after she crushed the fruit he had left to ripen.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai in quoted speech
claims.note: This is Kāyasandihai’s account of the curse.

claims.subject: tamil_later_kayasandihai
claims.summary: Kāyasandihai says she traveled from Kānchanapuram with her husband Kānchanan.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_kanchanan
claims.summary: Kāyasandihai identifies Kānchanan as a Vidyādhara from her world.
claims.speaker: Kāyasandihai
claims.note: This predicate records the stated celestial class, not a kinship relation.

claims.subject: tamil_manimekalai_heroine
claims.summary: After Kāyasandihai leaves, Manimekalai worships the goddess Muthiyāl in the Ulaga Aravi temple.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_manimekalai_heroine
claims.summary: Manimekalai also worships the Kaṇṭil Pāvai in the temple.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: The Pāvai is treated as the speaking temple figure/deity described later, not as a human character.

claims.subject: indra
claims.summary: Chitrāpathi cites Indra’s desire for Ahalya, Gautama’s wife, and says Indra was cursed with a thousand eyes.
claims.speaker: Chitrāpathi in quoted speech
claims.note: A rhetorical myth example in Chitrāpathi’s argument, not an episode involving the epic’s characters.

claims.subject: tamil_later_ahalya
claims.summary: Chitrāpathi identifies Ahalya as the wife of the sage Gautama.
claims.speaker: Chitrāpathi in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: root_agni
claims.summary: Chitrāpathi says Agni desired the seven wives of sages but did not consummate that desire.
claims.speaker: Chitrāpathi in quoted speech
claims.note: The passage says Agni desired the wives as a group; it does not narrate a union with Arundhati.

claims.subject: tamil_later_sukhadevi
claims.summary: Chitrāpathi identifies Sukhadevi as Agni’s wife.
claims.speaker: Chitrāpathi in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_sukhadevi
claims.summary: Chitrāpathi says Sukhadevi took the form of six of the sages’ seven wives, with Arundhati excluded.
claims.speaker: Chitrāpathi in quoted speech
claims.note: The six unnamed women are not expanded into guessed identities.

claims.subject: tamil_later_sukhadevi
claims.summary: Chitrāpathi says Sukhadevi, in the assumed forms of six wives, made love with Agni.
claims.speaker: Chitrāpathi in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_kanthil_pavai
claims.summary: The temple figure tells Manimekalai what happened to Udayakumaran and predicts her release from prison.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_udayakumaran
claims.summary: Kanthil Pāvai tells Manimekalai that the prince Udayakumaran was born as her former husband Rāgulan in this birth.
claims.speaker: Kanthil Pāvai, as translated by Hart
claims.note: Rebirth/alias edge stated by the speaking temple figure; Udayakumaran and Rāgulan remain separate person nodes.

claims.subject: tamil_brahmadarman
claims.summary: The figure recounts that, in the former birth as Lakshmi, she and Rāgulan hosted the sage Brahmadarman.
claims.speaker: Kanthil Pāvai, as translated by Hart
claims.note: Lakshmi is the heroine’s previous-birth name as in the earlier batch; this is an embedded past-life episode.

claims.subject: tamil_ragulan
claims.summary: Rāgulan kills the unnamed cook after the cook drops and spills the food intended for Brahmadarman.
claims.speaker: Kanthil Pāvai, as translated by Hart
claims.note: The cook is unnamed; no person node is created.

claims.subject: tamil_later_marudi
claims.summary: After a younger son of Kānthan approaches her, Mārudi goes to the Buddha sadukkam and prays to its deity, a Bhūdam.
claims.speaker: Sages recounting the story to the king
claims.note: The son is unnamed and is not identified with either the unnamed son in another episode or any named prince.

claims.subject: tamil_later_bhudam_marudi
claims.summary: The Bhūdam tells Mārudi that Kānthan will learn of his son’s conduct and kill him; the sages report that the prediction comes true.
claims.speaker: Sages recounting the story to the king
claims.note: Kānthan’s son is unnamed. This claim records the prediction and outcome, not an identity for the son.

claims.subject: tamil_later_dharmadattan
claims.summary: The sage says Dharmadattan and Visākai are uncle’s son and daughter, respectively.
claims.speaker: A sage recounting the story to the king
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_visakai
claims.summary: Visākai says she will not marry Dharmadattan in this birth but will be his wife in a future birth.
claims.speaker: A sage recounting Visākai’s speech to the king
claims.note: This is a future-birth promise, not a marriage in the narrated present.

claims.subject: tamil_later_visakai
claims.summary: Visākai asks the goddess figure on a pillar to remove the town’s gossip about her.
claims.speaker: A sage recounting the story to the king
claims.note: This canto names a pillar figure but does not identify it as the Kaṇṭil Pāvai; keep those figures separate.

claims.subject: tamil_later_dharmadattan
claims.summary: After returning to their town, Dharmadattan and Visākai perform acts of charity together.
claims.speaker: A sage recounting the story to the king
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_rajamadevi
claims.summary: After Udayakumaran’s death, the queen visits the elder counselor Vāsantavai, who admonishes her.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_rajamadevi
claims.summary: Rājamādevi tells the king that Manimekalai has done nothing wrong and requests that he release her from prison.
claims.speaker: Narrator and Rājamādevi in quoted speech
claims.note: Rājamādevi requests the release; a separate claim records the unnamed king as the person who carries it out.

claims.subject: tamil_later_rajamadevi
claims.summary: Manimekalai addresses the queen as the mother of her former-life husband Rāgulan, now Udayakumaran.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai in quoted speech
claims.note: The mother/son relation is explicit; the previous-life relation is the heroine’s narrative account.

claims.subject: tamil_later_nedumudikkilli
claims.summary: Chitrāpathi identifies Nedumudikkilli as Udayakumaran’s father.
claims.speaker: Narrator and Chitrāpathi’s embedded story
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_nedumudikkilli
claims.summary: In Chitrāpathi’s story, Nedumudikkilli meets and becomes fascinated by Peelivalai at the shore.
claims.speaker: Chitrāpathi recounting the story to the queen
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_peelivalai
claims.summary: The Jain sage tells Nedumudikkilli that Peelivalai is the daughter of Valaivanan, king of the Nāga country.
claims.speaker: The Jain sage in Chitrāpathi’s embedded story
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_peelivalai
claims.summary: The Jain sage identifies Vāsa Mayilai as Peelivalai’s mother.
claims.speaker: The Jain sage in Chitrāpathi’s embedded story
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_peelivalai
claims.summary: An astrologer predicts Peelivalai will love a prince of the Sun dynasty and bear a boy; the passage does not name the child’s father.
claims.speaker: The Jain sage in Chitrāpathi’s embedded story
claims.note: The Jain sage recounts an astrologer’s prediction. The text does not explicitly identify the predicted prince as Nedumudikkilli.

claims.subject: tamil_later_nedumudikkilli
claims.summary: The Jain sage warns Nedumudikkilli that he must not forget Indra’s festival, citing Indra’s curse and the threatened loss of the city.
claims.speaker: The Jain sage in Chitrāpathi’s embedded story
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_punniyarajan
claims.summary: Manimekalai tells Punniyarājan he was Āputhiran; the Peedihai later shows him the same former birth.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai; then narrator
claims.note: Keep tamil_later_punniyarajan and tamil_apputhiran as separate IDs linked by rebirth/alias. The passage supports this identity directly.

claims.subject: tamil_later_dharmasavagan
claims.summary: Punniyarājan bows to sage Dharmasāvagan, who teaches him about deeds, impermanence, suffering, and release.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_kanjugan
claims.summary: The translation identifies Kanjugan as Punniyarājan’s guard.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_bhumichandran
claims.summary: Bhumichandran, described as childless, raises Punniyarājan as his son.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_amarasundari
claims.summary: Amarasundari is identified as Punniyarājan’s stepmother.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_sali
claims.summary: Amarasundari tells Punniyarājan that Sāli abandoned him as a baby in his former birth as Āputhiran.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: The abandonment is reported to Punniyarājan as part of his prior-birth account; Sāli is not the mother in Punniyarājan’s current birth.

claims.subject: tamil_later_janamithran
claims.summary: Janamithran is identified as the king’s minister and asks Punniyarājan to remain until the country is secured.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: indra
claims.summary: Manimekalai reports Aravanar’s explanation that the Peedihai will speak about births only when Indra instructs it.
claims.speaker: Manimekalai recounting Aravanar’s words
claims.note: This is reported speech within the epic, not a separate witnessed scene between Indra and the Peedihai.

claims.subject: tamil_later_sindadevi
claims.summary: Punniyarājan recalls his previous life as Āputhiran, when Sindādevi gave him the inexhaustible vessel to feed the hungry.
claims.speaker: Punniyarājan in quoted speech
claims.note: Explicit prior-birth episode; preserve Punniyarājan and Āputhiran as separate nodes.

claims.subject: tamil_kannagi
claims.summary: Manimekalai visits the statues of her parents Kovalan and Kannagi; the statue presented as the goddess Kannagi speaks to her.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Keep the mother/person node and the speaking deified/statue node distinct; this edge records the epic’s representation.

claims.subject: tamil_later_goddess_kannagi
claims.summary: The speaking goddess Kannagi says that in a previous birth she was Sangaman’s wife.
claims.speaker: Goddess Kannagi in quoted speech
claims.note: A narrated previous-birth relation; do not merge Sangaman with Kovalan or treat this as a present-life marriage.

claims.subject: tamil_later_vasu
claims.summary: The goddess Kannagi’s story says Vasu and Kumaran ruled Singapuram and Kabilai, respectively.
claims.speaker: Goddess Kannagi in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_kumaran
claims.summary: The goddess Kannagi’s story says Kumaran ruled Kabilai.
claims.speaker: Goddess Kannagi in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_vasu
claims.summary: The two related kings Vasu and Kumaran are said to have fought one another.
claims.speaker: Goddess Kannagi in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_bharathan
claims.summary: Bharathan tells the king that Sangaman is a spy after guards report that he is selling ornaments.
claims.speaker: Goddess Kannagi in quoted speech
claims.note: The poem does not name which of the two kings hears the accusation; no king is assigned as the executioner in this claim.

claims.subject: tamil_later_madhurapuri
claims.summary: The goddess Madhurāpuri tells Sangaman’s wife not to curse the city and warns that the act will bring punishment.
claims.speaker: Goddess Kannagi in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; it is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_later_goddess_kannagi
claims.summary: The goddess Kannagi says that in the prior-birth story she ignored Madhurāpuri’s warning and destroyed the city by cursing it.
claims.speaker: Goddess Kannagi in quoted speech
claims.note: Hart’s English passage calls it “the city” without naming it here; the node remains distinct from Singapuram.

claims.subject: tamil_later_cenkuttuvan
claims.summary: The translation says Cenkuttuvan defeats the northern Kanaga Vijayar and other kings, who carry divine stones for a statue of Kannagi.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: Kanaga Vijayar is a collective of kings in Hart’s translation, not a single individual.

claims.subject: tamil_later_kanthil_pavai
claims.summary: The Kaṇṭil Pāvai tells Kānchanan that the figure he took for Kāyasandihai is actually Manimekalai in disguise.
claims.speaker: Kanthil Pāvai in quoted speech
claims.note: The statue/deity speaks; it is not the same person as Muthiyāl or the goddess Maṇimēkalai.

claims.subject: tamil_later_kanchanan
claims.summary: Kānchanan mistakes Manimekalai in Kāyasandihai’s form for his wife and kills Udayakumaran with his sword.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: The mistaken identity is explicit; Kānchanan kills the prince, not his wife.

claims.subject: tamil_later_muthiyal
claims.summary: The goddess’s temple statue tells Udayakumaran that his vow to possess Manimekalai cannot be fulfilled.
claims.speaker: The statue of Muthiyāl in quoted speech
claims.note: Muthiyāl and Kaṇṭil Pāvai remain distinct temple figures.

claims.subject: tamil_later_nakka_saranar
claims.summary: A heavenly voice tells Āthirai that Sāduvan survived and reached the hills where Nakka Saranar Nāgar lives.
claims.speaker: Voice from the sky, quoted by the narrator
claims.note: Kept distinct from the plural Nakka Sāranars who later find Sāduvan and take him to Gurumahan.

claims.subject: tamil_later_peelivalai
claims.summary: Deepathilahai says Peelivalai gave her baby boy to the rug merchant Kambala Chetti and asked him to take the child with him.
claims.speaker: Deepathilahai in quoted speech
claims.note: The child is unnamed; no independent claim about the boy’s father is added here.

claims.subject: tamil_later_kambala_chetti
claims.summary: Kambala Chetti leaves the island carrying Peelivalai’s baby; the ship sinks on the day he departs.
claims.speaker: Deepathilahai in quoted speech
claims.note: The Tamil verse names the rug merchant Kambala Chetti; Hart renders the role in English as “a rug merchant.” Do not equate him with Chandradathan from canto 16.

claims.subject: tamil_later_peelivalai_story_king
claims.summary: After the ship carrying Peelivalai’s child sinks, the surviving sailors tell the unnamed king that his son was aboard.
claims.speaker: Deepathilahai in quoted speech
claims.note: Hart’s passage leaves this king unnamed; no identity is inferred from an editorial subsection title or from canto 24’s Nedumudikkilli episode.

claims.subject: tamil_later_chola_king_23
claims.summary: After Rājamādevi asks for Manimekalai’s release, the king frees her and the queen takes her to the palace.
claims.speaker: Narrator
claims.note: The king is unnamed in this passage; his identity as Udayakumaran’s father is explicit in the surrounding narrative.

claims.subject: tamil_later_manmuhan
claims.summary: Aravanar’s account says the sage Manmuhan had a cow with golden horns and feet that gave milk generously.
claims.speaker: Aravanar in quoted speech
claims.note: Passage-level relationship from Hart’s English translation; this is a narrative witness, not independent historical evidence.

claims.subject: tamil_apputhiran
claims.summary: Aravanar says Āputhiran, who died on Manipallavam, was born again from the womb of Manmuhan’s cow.
claims.speaker: Aravanar in quoted speech
claims.note: This is Āputhiran’s rebirth within the embedded story; it is not the later Punniyarājan birth narrated in cantos 24–25.
